output.myth: When the snow lets go of the cliffs, the goats go mad with spring and want every ledge at once. Hesk, who keeps count, showed the herders how to lift a crook and turn the flock uphill, where the wind keeps the grass short and the rot cannot follow. That crook is Hulun. Its hook hangs in the north over the gull-road, and its foot is the bright stone at the bottom of the sky. Ennu carved the shaft from a goat's shin, which the goat has not forgiven. When Aun cut the string he took one nanny up with him by mistake, and she is still up there, working the Lamp Road for the good grass. Orrun does not say whether the sea needs turning too. Go up after her, the old women say, and keep your count.
output.verse:
Hulun turns the goats
the last snow loosens its hold
up to the green height
